content.title: March Madness stars front marquee sneaker companies as NIL reshapes campaign strategies
content.text: One of the “biggest college stars” headed into the NCAA men’s basketball tournament and this summer’s NBA Draft is BYU F AJ Dybantsa. Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The rise of formal endorsement deals between footwear companies and amateur athletes has “created a new landscape” in which teenage talent “leads brand campaigns and fronts marquee sneaker models,” according to Ian Stonebrook of ANDSCAPE. The “two biggest college stars” headed into the NCAA men’s basketball tournament are BYU F AJ Dybantsa and Univ. of Kansas G Darryn Peterson. Each has had an NIL deal since age 16, with Peterson joining Adidas in 2023 and Dybantsa signing with Nike in 2024. Adidas has “positioned itself as a major player in NIL” this March Madness, thanks to “numerous deals done years prior.” St. John’s Univ. G Ian Jackson and Univ. of Louisville G Mikel Brown Jr. both “became Adidas NIL athletes in 2024 when ascending at Overtime Elite.” Meanwhile, Univ. of Oklahoma G Aaliyah Chavez has “emerged as an ambassador” for Nike’s new Kobe Brand since signing in 2025. But numerous NCAA standouts “exist in a grayer space.” LSU G Flau’jae Johnson will “play in school-supplied Nikes” in the NCAA women’s tournament despite having an NIL deal with Puma. Univ. of Arkansas G Darius Acuff Jr. will also “lead a Nike-backed school” despite being signed to Reebok. Both are among a “slew of stars signed to NIL shoe deals that cross party lines regarding school sponsorship rights” (ANDSCAPE, 3/18).MONEY MAKERS: MODERN RETAIL’s Julia Waldow wrote companies are “racing to sign college basketball players and feature them in marketing materials” as the NCAA tournament gets underway. Jordan Brand announced it was working with Univ. of Connecticut G Azzi Fudd, while NYX Professional Makeup said that it was joining forces with UCLA C Lauren Betts and made her “the face of the latest iteration” of its “Make Them Look” campaign, which the brand is “promoting online and on social media.” On Monday, Freddy’s, a custard and burger chain, “announced deals with 10 collegiate athletes in Arizona, North Carolina, Tennessee and Texas.” Men’s care brand Every Man Jack is partnering with Univ. of Michigan G Elliot Cadeau “on several initiatives.” Cadeau will be “appearing in social media campaigns” for the brand’s new Full Court collection of under-$10 deodorants and body washes, available exclusively at Target (MODERN RETAIL, 3/18).Sponsored contentAdditional SectionsAwards & HonorsBettingCollegesDataEvents and Attractions Exec TransactionsFacilitiesFinanceFranchisesInternationalLabor and AgentsLeagues and Governing BodiesLegal and GovernanceMarketingMediaOlympicsOpinionPeople and Pop CultureSports and SocietyTechWomen's SportsSBJ TV
